text:
evan: Heads up — noticed a regression on staging: a spike of OOMs when many long-chat requests hit the KV cache + large batching. Looks like fragmentation + aggressive prefill is exhausting workspace pools.

priya: Ugh. Can you paste the trace or perf log? :eyes:

evan: Pasting tail of gpu logs and allocator stats.
```
2026-03-15T10:12:18Z gpu0 OOM alloc=3.2G free=512M fragments=27
pool_stats: workspace_total=8G workspace_used=7.6G slab_free=384M
kv_cache: total_entries=120k avg_entry_size=18k prefill_bytes=1.3G
batching: active_batches=42 avg_seq=1024
```

julia: That fragmentation count is the killer. Looks like prefill copies are creating many small allocations that the slab allocator can't coalesce.

kai: Two quick levers: reduce prefill window (truncate prefix prefill), or introduce per-request KV cap so a single request can't reserve >X bytes. Which is easier to experiment with?

priya: Per-request caps are low-risk. We can also add a reclaim pass that walks inactive KV segments and returns buffers to a fallback LRU pool.

evan: I ran a microbenchmark toggling per-request cap=64MB vs 256MB. Results: 64MB eliminated OOMs but increased decode latency 5-8% p95 for long sequences. 256MB still had occasional OOMs under high concurrency.

julia: Could we do hybrid: prefill only up to the per-request cap, but allow decode-path streaming to allocate transiently with immediate free when tokenized? So prefill controlled, streaming stays.

kai: That fits with allocator tuning — reserve a small fast slab for streaming (short-lived buffers) and a separate larger slab for prefill (long-lived). Then eviction is just slab->LRU eviction rather than granular free which causes fragmentation.

perf-bot: CI/job/kv-stress-03 finished: peak-memory=7.8G, p95-latency=312ms, ooms=0 (after cap=64MB patch).

priya: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) implement slab split + fast-reclaim path, 2) add metrics: per-request-kv-bytes and per-slab-fragmentation. Both will help observability for canary.

evan: I'll prototype allocator change. Quick sketch:
```
// allocator config pseudocode
allocator {
  slabs: [ {name: "hot", size: 1G, max_obj=64MB, eviction_policy: fifo},
           {name: "cold", size: 7G, max_obj=512MB, eviction_policy: lru} ]
  reclaim_threshold: 0.9
}
```
Plan: hot slab used for streaming/decode allocations; cold slab for prefill/kv. Reclaim_threshold triggers background compaction when free <10%.

julia: For compaction, consider a deferred coalesce that runs at low load. Do not run during p95-critical windows. Also add a per-request cap metric that triggers a soft-fail (log + sampling) when exceeded.

kai: Perf experiment idea: try prefill-on-decode (allocate only when decoding) vs prefill-ahead. Run both under mixed workload of short chat and long chat. We'll log fragmentation after each scenario.

evan: Ran that baseline: prefill-ahead gave 12% better throughput in steady state but fragmentation grows linearly. Prefill-on-decode reduces fragmentation but lowers throughput, and saw a 10% higher token latency due to more lock contention.

priya: Sounds like a classic tradeoff. My recommendation: default to prefill-ahead with enforced per-request cap + slab split + periodic compaction. For enterprise tier we can expose a knob to prefer lower p95 vs lower cost.

perf-bot: perf/regressions/compare-180123: prefill-ahead+cap=64MB+slab-split -> ooms=0, p95 latency +3%, throughput -4%.

julia: That seems acceptable. Move to canary on dedicated cluster A. Add automatic fallback: if ooms>0 for 5min, fall back to prefill-on-decode for new requests.

evan: I'll open the RFC and a small PR with the allocator prototype and metric emission. Will include a simple script to replay the kv-stress trace so SRE can validate.

kai: Ping me on the PR. Also add a perf test tag so perf-bot runs the stress harness automatically. :thumbsup:

priya: Thanks team. Good to have concrete numbers. Let's not forget to add an integration test that simulates many small frees to catch regression on fragmentation.

evan: Agreed. Draft PR coming in ~2 days.

perf-bot: link: ci/reports/kv-eviction-experiment-180123.html :rocket:
